title: stop.result.v1: what a Stop answers
description: The answer of run.stop when the run exists. THE LEGACY ANSWER is exactly what the daemon answers today and stays valid: code 'stopped' or 'pending', 'state' with the same word, 'repeat' on a stopped answer, 'reason' on a pending one, and 'recorded' only when it is false. THE ADDITIONS are optional, and each is added to the daemon's answers by the lane that owns Stop, in a versioned step of its own, never by the lane that wrote this schema: the code 'ended', and the fields 'attestation', 'containment_level', 'claim' and 'fence'. Until then no answer carries them, and the answer for a run id that was never registered stays today's. MEANINGS, frozen: 'stopped' means the run's removal was attested (today by proof 'empty'; by 'removed' once that is added). 'ended' means the run had already ended before this Stop, and this call stopped nothing; it never implies a verified removal. 'pending' means neither is established. A client that meets a code or a proof it does not know treats the run as NOT stopped. A client that meets a 'claim' it does not know shows nothing stronger than the weakest claim it does know.

state.description: The same word as 'code'. It is kept because today's answer carries both.

repeat.description: False for the first Stop asked of a run. True when a Stop had already been asked: the run was already stopped, or an earlier Stop was pending and this one confirmed it. It does not mean 'the run had already stopped'.

recorded.description: Present only when it is false: the answer could not be written to the registry. An absent field means the write landed. 'Not recorded' is its own fact: the cleanup answer above is still true.

pending_reason.description: Why a Stop is not confirmed. cgroup_populated: a process is still in the cgroup. confirm_timeout: the check did not finish in time. confirm_unknown: the check gave no usable answer. member_alive: a recorded member process is still alive. cgroup_changed: the record moved to another cgroup while the Stop ran. cgroup_unknown: the launch has not recorded a cgroup yet, so the Stop is kept as an intent. cleanup_error:<Name>: the cleanup layer raised the named error.

attestation.description: PROVISIONAL, the Stop lane's. The evidence a 'stopped' answer rests on, carried in the answer itself. proof 'empty': the cgroup at this path was read empty. proof 'removed': the cgroup directory recorded at launch, identified by cgroup_identity, no longer exists or is a different directory. time is when that was observed. cgroup_identity is null only when none was recorded at launch, which is possible only with proof 'empty'. A client that meets any other proof treats the run as NOT stopped.

containment_level.description: PROVISIONAL, the Stop lane's, and it waits on a decision. How the run was contained when it launched. host_integrated: the engine ran as the daemon's own user in a delegated unit (the only level that exists today). engine_user: the engine ran as a separate operating-system user. contained: the unit also ran with the verified restrictions that lane defines.

claim.description: PROVISIONAL, the Stop lane's. The key of the sentence a surface shows for this Stop. No surface writes its own wording. cgroup_empty_whole_run_unverified: the supervised cgroup was read empty; nothing is claimed about a process that left it. cgroup_removed_whole_run_unverified: the supervised cgroup is gone; nothing is claimed about a process that left it. ended_before_stop_removal_unverified: the run had ended before the Stop; this call stopped nothing and no removal was verified.

fence.description: PROVISIONAL, the Stop lane's. Whether a launch of this run can still be dispatched. 'fenced': no later launch under this run id and incarnation will start. 'dispatched': a launch had already been handed to the unit manager when the fence was set. incarnation counts the launches under one run id.
